questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of Redis Sentinel?

options.text: To shard data across many primaries
To provide high availability for a primary/replica setup via monitoring and automatic failover
To compress data in memory
To encrypt client connections

questions.explanation: Sentinel monitors a primary/replica deployment and, on failure, promotes a replica and redirects clients — high availability, not sharding.

options.text: How many keys can be stored
How many Sentinels must agree the primary is down (ODOWN) before failover
The number of replicas allowed
The TCP port Sentinel uses

questions.explanation: The quorum is the number of Sentinels that must agree the primary is objectively down (ODOWN) to trigger a failover.

questions.prompt: Which statements about Sentinel are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: You should run an odd number of Sentinels, at least three, on separate hosts
Clients can ask Sentinel for the current primary's address (service discovery)
SDOWN is one Sentinel's view; ODOWN requires the quorum to agree
Sentinel shards the keyspace across nodes

questions.explanation: Odd number ≥3, service discovery, and the SDOWN→ODOWN progression are all correct. Sentinel does NOT shard data — that's Cluster.

questions.prompt: How does Sentinel differ from Redis Cluster?

options.text: They are identical
Sentinel provides HA for a single non-sharded primary; Cluster shards data across many primaries and also handles failover
Cluster cannot fail over; Sentinel can
Sentinel stores more data per node

questions.explanation: Sentinel keeps one primary available (no sharding); Cluster splits data across 16384 slots on multiple primaries with built-in failover.

questions.prompt: When enough Sentinels agree the primary is down, it is declared ______ Down (objectively). (one word for the O)
questions.explanation: ODOWN (Objectively Down) is reached when the quorum of Sentinels agrees the primary is unreachable — the trigger for failover.

questions.prompt: Why is running only two Sentinels risky?

options.text: Two Sentinels use too much memory
Authorizing a failover needs a majority of Sentinels, and a single failure or partition can break a two-node majority
Sentinel requires exactly one instance
Two Sentinels cannot monitor replicas

questions.explanation: A failover requires a majority of Sentinels to agree. With only two, losing one (or a partition) prevents forming a majority, stalling recovery — so run an odd number, at least three.
